characters.name: Owen Pritchard
characters.role: Sheriff of Mercy Crossing; Old Warden
characters.looks: Long, grey, and folded into his chair like a carpenter's rule. A Warden's star worn smooth. A right hand that shakes until it is holding something.
characters.voice: One instruction at a time, and a dry joke he does not wait to see land. Says a man's whole name when he means to hang him and his first name when he means to feed him.
characters.wants: To hand the valley to somebody better than himself before the shaking gets to his gun hand.
characters.fears: That the last lawful thing he ever does will be signing the valley over to whichever flag gets to his porch first.
characters.secret: He hanged the wrong man in the spring of '98 and has kept the rope in his desk ever since. He has not hanged anybody since, whatever the Cutters believe.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks the Dominion are still Wardens underneath, and that Amos Brigg can be shamed.
knows: Gantt was bringing him a name and would not put it on paper
Three towns going under in one month is not weather
Vane has kept this town fed through two bad winters
does_not_know: Who Gantt meant
That Vane's money is behind the three roads
Anything of what is under the mountains

ties.what: The son he never had and the deputy he should not have hired
Twenty years of supper together. Has never once asked to see the books
Rode with him as a young Warden. Brigg still calls him Sergeant
She sat the bench the day he hanged the wrong man

characters.name: Silas Vane
characters.role: Merchant at Mercy Crossing; keeps two sets of books
characters.looks: Neat as a hymn-book. Sleeve garters, a pencil behind the ear, spectacles he polishes when he is lying and when he is not, so that nobody can tell.
characters.voice: Courteous, exact, amused. Gives a figure where another man would give an oath. Never raises his voice and never repeats an offer.
characters.wants: A valley too poor, too slow and too far apart to be worth any army's while.
characters.fears: A flag over his door. Any flag.
characters.secret: He has paid for a pulled rail, a held barge and a chained mine, every month, for six years, out of silver that comes down from Blackstone Station from a client he has never seen.
characters.wrong_about: He believes he is the one doing the buying.
knows: Exactly what every family in Mercy Crossing owes and to whom
That the silver comes sealed, by the night freight, and that asking who sends it would end it
What a Dominion garrison did to the last town that could afford one
does_not_know: Who his client is or what they want the quiet for
That the Cutters killed Gantt's errand by accident and not on his order
Anything of what is under the mountains

ties.what: The only man whose good opinion he would pay for and cannot buy
She keeps his second set of books and would shoot the first person who read them
Lets him sign for freight because nobody would suspect him of anything

characters.name: Jonah Talbot
characters.role: Deputy at the town gate
characters.looks: All elbows and good intentions. A star too big for the shirt and a revolver he has cleaned more often than fired.
characters.voice: Fast, earnest, corrects himself halfway through. Quotes Pritchard without noticing he is doing it.
characters.wants: To be sent somewhere that matters.
characters.fears: That when it comes to it his hands will do what Pritchard's do.
characters.secret: He has never shot at a person and has told three different girls that he has.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks the star is what stops a bullet.
knows: Every face that has come through the gate in two years
Which of the gate guard takes Vane's money to wave a wagon through
does_not_know: What Pritchard keeps in the desk
How fast a man like Dole decides

ties.what: Would walk into a fire for him and probably will
Has been in love with her since she ran the yard gate on a handcar to win a bet

characters.name: Reese Dunmore
characters.role: Leads the Tellico Cutters; by Chapter 2 he is on a rope or under the ground
characters.looks: A good coat gone bad, a logger's shoulders, and a grin with a debt behind it.
characters.voice: Friendly as a card-sharp. Offers shares. Calls everyone partner until the moment he does not.
characters.wants: One score big enough to stop.
characters.fears: Hanging. He has seen it done badly.
characters.secret: The Cutters were not robbing a wagon for its own sake. They were paid in silver to wait on the Tellico road for whoever walked away from a train carrying a marshal's pouch, and the wagon was to pass the time.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks whoever paid him will buy him off the rope.
knows: The man who hired him paid in stamped silver and never showed his face
The train was expected to come off the rails that morning
does_not_know: Who the man was
What was in the pouch

ties.what: She has his neck on her docket
Has sold him stolen goods for years and thinks that makes them friends

characters.name: Nell Fenwick
characters.role: Wagon owner on the Tellico road; speaks for the small carriers
characters.looks: Weathered square, a drover's whip coiled at the belt, and one finger short on the left hand from a brake she did not let go of.
characters.voice: Prices everything out loud, including people. Laughs once, late.
characters.wants: A road she can drive without paying four people for the privilege.
characters.fears: Owing anybody.
characters.secret: She has carried sealed freight for Vane for three years and has never opened one box, and it has started to keep her awake.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks not looking is the same as not knowing.
knows: Which freight on the valley roads is Vane's and which only says so
That the Cutters were waiting for something that was not her wagon
does_not_know: What is in the sealed boxes
Who Vane answers to

ties.what: Her best customer and the reason she cannot afford a second wagon
Voted for her and would do it again, grumbling

characters.name: Ada Pike
characters.role: Gunsmith at Mercy Crossing; judges the beef shoot
characters.looks: Burn scars to the elbow, a jeweller's glass on a cord, and a ledger of every gun she has ever mended.
characters.voice: Parts, tolerances, and a short verdict. Warms up exactly one degree at a time.
characters.wants: To see one good shot before she dies that she did not have to teach.
characters.fears: Her work in the wrong hands, which is most hands.
characters.secret: She cut the silver mould. Twelve years ago a stranger paid her a year's keep to make a bullet mould for a calibre nobody carries, and she has known since the fair what it was for.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks a tool is innocent.
knows: The silver case from the bell-rail came out of a mould with her mark filed off it
The yard has bought no brake shoes from her since spring
does_not_know: The stranger's name
Where he is

ties.what: Made his mould. Never saw his face in daylight
Mended her rifle for nothing and would not say why

characters.name: Corwin Haskell
characters.role: Freight agent; signs the receiving page at Mercy Crossing
characters.looks: Ink to the wrist, a celluloid collar, and the stoop of a man who has been expecting to be blamed since boyhood.
characters.voice: Careful to the point of pain. Says who received what, from whom, at what hour, and stops.
characters.wants: The count to come out right.
characters.fears: A crowd.
characters.secret: He has known for a year that one crate in twenty that he signs for weighs like metal and is entered as dry goods. He weighed one. He wrote the weight down and hid the page.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks keeping the page makes him honest.
knows: The night freight leaves sealed crates for Vane that come from up the line past Iron Junction
Their true weight
does_not_know: What is in them
That the page could hang Vane or save him

ties.what: Owes him his job and is afraid of what else
Would tell him everything if he were asked a direct question

characters.name: Augusta Lockridge
characters.role: Yardmaster of Iron Junction; everyone calls her Gussie
characters.looks: Big, slow and immaculate, in a conductor's coat with the braid kept up. Smokes a clay pipe. Runs the yard from a dining car set on the roundhouse turntable so that her window can be turned to face whoever is coming.
characters.voice: Riverboat manners over a foreman's lungs. Calls everybody honey and has had men flogged. Talks about trains as if they were kin.
characters.wants: The line open. Nothing else has ever been real to her.
characters.fears: A day with no train on the board.
characters.secret: When Ostrander was given up for dead no inspector would come out to a line that kills inspectors, so she took his stamp out of his desk and has been passing her own trains ever since. Line 14 was hers. So was the train the stranger walked away from.
characters.wrong_about: She believes every one of those signatures saved more people than it killed, and has never done the sum.
knows: Which cars on her roster should not be moving
That somebody with a yard pass is telling the Black Rail her timetable
does_not_know: That Ostrander is alive
That he is the one pulling her rails

ties.what: Worked beside him nineteen years when he was her inspector. Read at his funeral
Raised her in the roundhouse and will not say she is proud

characters.name: Wilhelmina Tarrow
characters.role: Driver of the Night Mail; called Billie
characters.looks: Soot to the hairline, a red bandanna, goggles pushed up, and a grin that should not be let near a regulator.
characters.voice: Fast, cheerful, profane about machinery and tender about nothing else. Bets on everything.
characters.wants: To drive something faster than Old Contrary before she is thirty or dead.
characters.fears: Being put on a desk.
characters.secret: She has known for months that the brake shoes on half the roster are scrap and has driven them anyway because Gussie asked.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks she is too quick to be caught by anything that runs on rails.
knows: Every grade, curve and soft spot between Iron Junction and Blackstone
That the rail in Sawtooth Cut is spread, not gone, and that a light engine at speed might clear it
does_not_know: Who Dole was
Whose stamp is on her running papers

ties.what: The nearest thing to a mother she has, and her employer, which is worse
Thinks he is sweet. Has not decided whether that is a compliment

characters.name: Ezekiel Dole
characters.role: Preacher Dole of the Black Rail; pulls rails and robs what falls
characters.looks: A tall ruin in a frock coat and a railwayman's cap, a hymnal chained to his belt, an inspector's brass gauge hung round his neck like a cross. Preaches from a flatcar with a lantern in each hand.
characters.voice: Scripture and track measurements in the same breath, in a voice that carries a quarter mile. Gentle with his own people. Never shouts; he does not need to.
characters.wants: Every signature on the Corridor line made true or made to bleed.
characters.fears: That he was right to sign all those years and wrong to stop.
characters.secret: He is R. Ostrander, Inspector of Way. He condemned the Greenwater trestle and was overruled, took the fever, was left for dead in a pest-house, and walked out of it with a new name and a congregation. He takes the silver that is offered for pulled rails because it buys powder. He would pull them for nothing.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks a wreck is a sermon and that the people in the cars are the congregation rather than the collection.
knows: Exactly which cars the yard has passed that should have been broken up
That somebody is still signing his dead name
That the silver comes from a station up the line with a square mark
does_not_know: That it is Gussie Lockridge signing it
Who sends the silver

ties.what: Nineteen years her inspector. Loved her a little. Will not forgive her
Takes his silver through a go-between and despises him

characters.name: Opal Starnes
characters.role: Ration warden of Greenwater
characters.looks: Small, bent and hard as a hickory root, in a man's oilskin. A brass ladle chained to her left wrist and a double shotgun she calls Second Helping.
characters.voice: Counts under her breath. Blesses people and threatens them in the same sentence. Has never been heard to ask twice.
characters.wants: Every mouth in Greenwater fed until the dogwood blooms, and then Lyle Hatcher's neck.
characters.fears: The day the ladle scrapes the bottom with the line still out the door.
characters.secret: She has been feeding the town a quarter short for three weeks and eating nothing herself to hide it. She will not see the dogwood either way.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks hanging Hatcher will fill a single bowl.
knows: To the cup what Greenwater has left
That the grain barge was seen lashed to the Queen of Tellico
does_not_know: That Hatcher was paid to hold it
How sick she is

ties.what: Dandled him as a baby. Means to hang him
Her grandson, and the only pilot she trusts

characters.name: Lyle Hatcher
characters.role: Owner of the sternwheeler Queen of Tellico; styles himself Commodore
characters.looks: A white linen suit gone green at the seams, a planter's hat, rings on fingers that have never done a day's work, and the best teeth on the river.
characters.voice: Warm, slow and delighted with himself. Quotes the law of salvage. Deals cards while he talks and never looks at his hands.
characters.wants: To be loved by a room.
characters.fears: Being ordinary, and drowning. He cannot swim.
characters.secret: He was paid in silver to hold the grain barge past first frost and then release it. He decided to sell it back by the cup instead, and has told the paymaster nothing.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks Greenwater will forgive him by spring because it always has.
knows: The letter of hire is in his strongbox under the faro table
The Queen's boiler should have been condemned ten years ago
does_not_know: Who the paymaster is
That Opal Starnes means it this time

ties.what: She raised him on the same ladle. He sends her flowers
Taught him the river and cheated him of his pay

characters.name: Mose Pruitt
characters.role: River pilot at Greenwater; called Catfish
characters.looks: Barefoot, sunburnt, a straw hat with a bite out of the brim, and a pole he handles like a third arm.
characters.voice: Lazy as slack water, then suddenly not. Names every rock in the river as if introducing relatives.
characters.wants: A boat of his own with his name on the paddle-box.
characters.fears: Hangman's Chute at night, which he has run twice and lied about once.
characters.secret: He helped tow the grain barge out to the Queen. He was told it was for safe keeping and paid a dollar, and has not told his grandmother.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks he can put it right without her ever knowing.
knows: Where the Queen's anchor chain is rusted through
The one line through the Chute that a loaded barge can take
does_not_know: What his grandmother is hiding
That Hatcher keeps a man on the barge at night

ties.what: Her grandson. Would rather drown than face her
Owed two seasons' wages and a boat

characters.name: Esther Quill
characters.role: Warden magistrate; rides circuit for the Dominion on a gallows wagon
characters.looks: A black bombazine dress, a man's top hat with the crown stove in, half-moon spectacles, and a wagon with a bench at one end and a beam at the other.
characters.voice: Dry, quick and merciless about grammar. Passes sentence the way another woman would give a recipe. Enjoys an argument and has never lost one she allowed.
characters.wants: Law that travels faster than the people who break it.
characters.fears: That the Dominion has stopped needing a judge and kept her for the hat.
characters.secret: She knows Pritchard's man in '98 was innocent. She knew it on the day. She let it stand because the town needed it finished.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks a sentence carried out is a matter closed.
knows: Brigg wants the pike, the gap and every town below it by winter
The condemned man on her wagon was paid in stamped silver
does_not_know: Whose silver
That the stranger at her wagon is the one the Cutters were waiting for

ties.what: They have not spoken of the spring of '98 in nineteen years
He signs her warrants and reads none of them

characters.name: Hobart Greer
characters.role: Mine captain of Red Hollow
characters.looks: Grey with rock dust that no longer washes off, a carbide lamp on a hard hat he wears indoors, and a firing key on a lanyard that he holds the way other men hold a rosary.
characters.voice: Low and reasonable. Explains too much. Says for the good of the Hollow before every terrible thing.
characters.wants: The Mouth shut for good and nobody ever to ask him what came up in the cage.
characters.fears: What knocked back.
characters.secret: He has silver in his desk, paid to keep the mine chained through winter. He would have chained it for nothing. He took the money so that there would be a reason he could say out loud.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks the eleven on the night shift are already dead, because he could not bear it otherwise.
knows: The night shift broke through into worked stone at the Nine level
The cage came up empty except for a lamp nobody in Red Hollow made
The charges are set and the key is round his neck
does_not_know: That the shift is alive
Who is on the other side of the stone

ties.what: Her husband is on the night shift. He cannot look at her
Has taken his silver and never met him

characters.name: Dinah Roark
characters.role: Hoist-woman at Red Hollow; leads the vigil at the Mouth
characters.looks: Broad-handed, red to the knees with Hollow mud, a baby on her hip and a pry bar over her shoulder.
characters.voice: Flat and patient, like somebody talking a mule across a bridge. Sings while she waits. Does not raise her voice until she swings.
characters.wants: The cage lowered. Now.
characters.fears: Hearing the knocking stop.
characters.secret: She can read the knocking. The night shift is tapping the hoist code for eleven men, bad air. And something is tapping it back to them, slowly, a beat behind, like a child learning.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks Greer is a coward. He is, but that is not why he chained the Mouth.
knows: How to run the hoist alone
That the chain on the Mouth is on the outside for a reason nobody has told her
does_not_know: What the night shift broke into
That Greer was paid

ties.what: Her husband's captain. Will kill him if the charges go
Has been answering her code through four hundred feet of rock without knowing her name

characters.name: Helga Dorn
characters.role: Gallery-warden of a Hearth House of the Stonebound; holds the stone door under Red Hollow
characters.looks: Short, heavy-shouldered, grey-eyed, in quilted leather and a collar of worked iron. A lamp that burns without smoke. Squints at a carbide flame as if it were rude.
characters.voice: Formal, slow, a little old-fashioned, as if she learned the language from documents. Measures before she speaks. Dry as slate once she decides you are not a thief.
characters.wants: The upper galleries of her House left alone, and the eleven strangers in her care off her hands before her own council decides what they are.
characters.fears: A mine captain with a firing key, and her own Forgers, who would answer a blast with one of their own.
characters.secret: Her House is nine families and failing. She came up to the door alone because there was nobody to send.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks the people above are one House with one head who can swear for all of them.
knows: The miners blasted into a gallery her people cut two hundred years ago
She has fed the night shift for three days and they have not once said thank you
The hoist code, now, more or less
does_not_know: How many people live in the valleys or who rules them
What the silver is or who the flags are

ties.what: The patient one who knocks. Dorn would like to meet her
The one who sent the lamp back up empty. Dorn took it for an insult

characters.name: Clara Whitcomb
characters.role: Speaker of the Compact; carries the first flag
characters.looks: A travelling suit with mud to the knee, an auctioneer's gavel through her belt, and a tally-book she writes in while people are still talking.
characters.voice: An auctioneer's patter slowed down for honest people. Funny, quick, and counting votes the whole time.
characters.wants: Every road in the valleys open and nobody's permission needed to use one.
characters.fears: That the big buyers in her own Compact want the same thing Vane wants, only with her name on it.
characters.secret: The Brass Consortium has already offered Vane a seat if he brings Mercy Crossing in quietly, and she has not told the small carriers.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks a fair rule enforces itself.
knows: Which carriers are a bad season from selling out
That Brigg has two companies a day's march from the fair
does_not_know: Whose silver is moving in the valley
What the courier was carrying

ties.what: Her conscience, on a wagon
Has outbid him twice and expects to be shot for it eventually

characters.name: Amos Brigg
characters.role: Colonel of the Dominion; carries the second flag
characters.looks: Iron-grey, shaved to the blood, in a Warden's long coat dyed black. One glove. Counts everything in a room on entering it.
characters.voice: Quiet, level, a schoolmaster's patience. Addresses people by what they are for. Has never been known to threaten; he informs.
characters.wants: One law from the gap to the river, and himself as the hand that holds it.
characters.fears: Disorder he was not consulted about.
characters.secret: His two companies have orders to take the camp-ground the moment anybody fires a shot at the fair. He did not arrange the shot. He only arranged to be ready for it.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks people who are safe are grateful.
knows: The strength of every town militia between here and Iron Junction
That Pritchard's hand shakes
does_not_know: Who fired
What is in the courier's case

ties.what: His old sergeant. Would rather not have to disarm him
Finds her useful and tiresome
Distrusts him on sight and cannot say why

characters.name: Tomas Belden
characters.role: Provisioning delegate of the Commonwealth; carries the third flag
characters.looks: Round, pink and tireless, in a good plain coat with a ration-pin on the lapel. Shakes every hand twice. Brings his own soup wagon and feeds anybody who will stand in line.
characters.voice: Warm as a stove. Says we where anybody else would say I. Never refuses; he defers to the committee.
characters.wants: Every pantry in the valleys on one list, and his office holding the list.
characters.fears: Being sent home having promised less than the others.
characters.secret: The Commonwealth's stores are a third of what he says. The soup is the offer.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks hungry people do not notice who is watching them eat.
knows: Greenwater is short
Exactly how many will follow a full pot
does_not_know: Why the grain went missing
That Vane has been outbidding him for six years

ties.what: Has offered her a seat on a ration committee. She set the dog on him
Old opponents who lunch together

characters.name: Lucien Grey
characters.role: Field surveyor for the Directorate; carries the fourth flag
characters.looks: Slight, pale, hatless in the rain, in a surveyor's oilskin with brass instruments in every pocket. Looks at people the way he looks at a slope.
characters.voice: Soft, exact and unhurried, with pauses in the wrong places as if listening to something else. Offers numbers as comfort.
characters.wants: Leave to set his instruments on the camp-ground hill, and a long look at the stranger from the wreck.
characters.fears: Nothing that he will show.
characters.secret: He knew the courier was coming and when. He did not stop the shot and he did not order it. He has met the stranger before, and can see that the stranger does not remember.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks a thing that can be predicted has been decided.
knows: Power could be brought back to the valleys inside a year, at a price he has not named
More about Blackstone Station than anyone else at the fair
does_not_know: How much the stranger has forgotten
That Edda Flint has been tracking his footprints as well as the shooter's

ties.what: Colleagues. Neither will say in what
Finds him simple and therefore dangerous

characters.name: Cassian Voss
characters.role: The man in the grey duster at the fair. Nobody there learns his name
characters.looks: Tall, easy, clean-shaven, in a dove-grey duster and a preacher's flat hat. One long pistol, worn low, with a bright sheen to the metal that he keeps turned away from the light.
characters.voice: Courteous, amused, a little sad. Compliments people accurately. Speaks of killing as weather.
characters.wants: The courier silent, and to see for himself what walked out of that train.
characters.fears: That he will be asked to do it again, to somebody he liked.
characters.secret: He knows the stranger. He was told the stranger was dead in the wreck, and came to the fair partly to be sure, and is not sure what he feels on finding otherwise.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks the stranger not knowing him is an act.
knows: The courier's road and the hour
The stranger's face, and how the stranger used to shoot
does_not_know: Why the stranger does not know him
That Ada Pike has kept the drawings of his mould

ties.what: Works the same trade for the same hand. Does not trust him
She has hunted him six years. He leaves her a cartridge case each time, out of respect
Paid her well and has never been back

characters.name: Edda Flint
characters.role: Bounty hunter; the shot to beat at the fair
characters.looks: Rangy, rain-coloured, a long rifle in a beaded scabbard, a string of spent silver cases round her neck that she does not explain, and boots re-soled more often than her patience.
characters.voice: Short sentences and long silences. Asks one question at a time and waits for all of the answer.
characters.wants: The man who leaves the silver cases, alive enough to ask why.
characters.fears: That when she has him she will find she already knows.
characters.secret: She recognised the stranger across the shooting line and said nothing, to see what the stranger would do.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks she is hunting one man.
knows: Seven killings, seven silver cases, six years
The shooter always leaves by water
does_not_know: The shooter's name
Whether the stranger is on his side or hers

ties.what: Six years behind him. He lets her get close
Trusts her with the rifle and nothing else

characters.name: Juno Three-Fords
characters.role: Courier out of the high country; dies at the fair
characters.looks: Lean as a fence rail, road-grey to the eyes, ears that turn a little toward a sound before her head does, and a tin map case chained to her wrist.
characters.voice: Out of breath and exact. Gives distances in fords and hours in pipes smoked.
characters.wants: To put the case into Pritchard's hand and sleep for a week.
characters.fears: Being followed by something she can hear and cannot see.
characters.secret: She was told to give the case to nobody but Pritchard, and if she could not, to throw it in the river.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks she lost the man behind her at the last ford.
knows: There are lights on Blackstone ridge where no town is
Trains run the dead line at night and stop at Blackstone Station
A number she was made to learn by heart and does not understand
does_not_know: What the number is
Who sent the man behind her

ties.what: Has carried for him twice before. He paid in boots

characters.name: Temperance Vickers
characters.role: Vane's bookkeeper, and the gun nobody knows he keeps
characters.looks: Grey dress, grey gloves, hair scraped back, and a ledger-box under her arm with a sawn-off in it where the cash tray should be.
characters.voice: Precise, colourless, polite. Corrects people's arithmetic. Does not bluff, because she has never needed to.
characters.wants: Mr Vane left alone to do his sums.
characters.fears: A world with no one in it who needs her to be exact.
characters.secret: She carries the silver down from the night freight herself. She has seen the hand that passes the box out of the car, and it wore a glove with a square mark stitched on the cuff.
characters.wrong_about: She thinks loyalty is the same as being right.
knows: Every entry in the black ledger, by heart
The night and the hour the next silver comes
does_not_know: Who the client is
That Vane has made provision for her in his will and none for himself

ties.what: He taught her double entry when she was a starving girl at his back door
Knows he weighed a crate. Has not told Vane, and does not know why not

characters.name: Tolly Granger
characters.role: Jobbing printer at Mercy Crossing; prints the ballad sheets
characters.looks: Ink-black to the elbow, a paper hat, one eye screwed up from setting type by candle, and a hand-press on a barrow.
characters.voice: Rhymes by accident. Sells while he talks. Calls every customer a patron of letters.
characters.wants: A story that sells out twice.
characters.fears: A slow week.
characters.secret: He prints Vane's handbills for nothing, and has never asked himself why Vane wants so many about the dangers of the roads.
characters.wrong_about: He thinks printing a thing is not the same as saying it.
knows: Everything that has happened in the valleys for a month, in ballad metre
What the stranger did on the Tellico road, or what is said
does_not_know: Which parts are true

ties.what: His best and quietest customer
Has been threatened with the lock-up for libel four times, fondly
